description: Health of the shared PostgreSQL cluster (`main`): instances, replication lag and WAL retention, throughput and cache, PVC/WAL storage, and transaction-ID wraparound risk. Metrics come from the instance manager on port 9187 (PodMonitor cloudnative-pg-instances).

panels.description: cnpg_collector_up summed across the cluster's instances. A drop means an instance manager stopped answering scrapes (the exporter is in-process with postgres, so this also tracks postgres being down).
panels.title: Instances up

panels.description: Which pod is not in recovery, i.e. the current primary. `cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery` is 1 on every standby, so the primary is the one that reads 0 - a standby promotion shows up here first.
panels.title: Primary

panels.description: Replicas the primary reports as streaming (`pg_stat_replication` rows). 0 on a 3-instance cluster means both standbys are disconnected — usually right after a failover while they re-sync.
panels.title: Streaming replicas

panels.description: Largest replay lag reported by any instance (`pg_last_wal_replay_lsn` vs primary LSN, in seconds).
panels.title: Max replication lag

panels.description: Client backends across all databases (summed over `state`) against `max_connections`. Near the limit, new clients get `FATAL: sorry, too many clients already`.
panels.title: Connections

panels.description: Size of the primary's pg_wal directory. Growth here without matching archiving means archive_command is failing or a replication slot is holding WAL.
panels.title: WAL on disk

panels.description: `pg_stat_replication` lag per standby, from the primary's point of view. These are intervals since the standby last wrote/flushed/replayed, so a steady non-zero replay lag with zero write lag is normal-ish; all three climbing means the standby is falling behind.
panels.title: Replication lag by replica (seconds)

panels.description: Byte distance between the primary's current LSN and what each standby has sent/received/written/flushed/replayed. This is the honest measure of 'how much would be lost right now if the primary died'.
panels.title: Replication bytes behind (bytes)

panels.description: Per-slot WAL retention. A slot that climbs without ever dropping pins WAL on the primary and will fill the WAL volume — the classic cause of 'disk full' on a Postgres primary. Values are per-pod snapshots: the primary's own rows are the ones that matter.
panels.title: WAL retained by replication slots (bytes)

panels.description: pg_wal segment accounting. `count` near `max` means WAL is at `max_wal_size` (checkpoint pressure); `ready` climbing means segments are waiting for archive_command.
panels.title: WAL files on disk (primary)

panels.description: Commit/rollback rate on the primary only (`* on(pod) group_left() (1 - in_recovery)` zeroes out the standbys, which report the same counters a moment later and would otherwise double-count).
panels.title: Transactions per second (primary)

panels.description: shared_buffers effectiveness: hits / (hits + reads) on the primary. A drop from ~99% to the 90s usually means a working set outgrew shared_buffers or a big sequential scan started.

targets.expr: 100 * sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~".*cloudnative-pg-instances",pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(pod) group_left() (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery)) / clamp_min(sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_hit{job=~".*cloudnative-pg-instances",pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(pod) group_left() (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery)) + sum(rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_blks_read{job=~".*cloudnative-pg-instances",pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(pod) group_left() (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery)), 0.001)

panels.title: Buffer cache hit ratio (primary, %)

panels.description: `requested` checkpoints mean WAL filled faster than `checkpoint_timeout` - each one is a write stall. Sustained requested checkpoints -> raise max_wal_size or lower the WAL generation rate.
panels.title: Checkpoints per hour

panels.description: Read volume per database on the primary. Useful to spot which app is behind a slow query storm or an unindexed scan.

targets.expr: topk(6, sum by (datname) (rate(cnpg_pg_stat_database_tup_fetched{job=~".*cloudnative-pg-instances",pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(pod) group_left() (1 - cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery)))

panels.title: Top databases by tuples fetched/s

panels.description: Deadlocks are lock-ordering bugs in an application and are always worth knowing about. Conflicts are standby queries cancelled by WAL replay (only if hot_standby_feedback is off).
panels.title: Deadlocks and conflicts per hour

panels.description: Filesystem utilisation of every CNPG PVC (data and `-wal` volumes). From kubelet, not from postgres: this is the number that predicts `disk full`. WAL volumes fill first when archiving stalls.
panels.title: PVC utilisation (%)

panels.description: `pg_database_size` per database, deduplicated with max by (datname) because all three instances report the same value.
panels.title: Database sizes (top 10)

panels.description: Oldest unfrozen XID across databases. Postgres refuses writes at 2^31-1 (~2.15e9) and CNPG will start logging warnings long before. 1.3e9 means autovacuum is not keeping up with freezing.
panels.title: Transaction ID age

panels.description: Same wraparound risk for multixacts (shared row locks). Threshold is 2^31-1 as well but multixacts age much faster under heavy FOR SHARE/KEY SHARE traffic.
panels.title: Multixact ID age

panels.description: 1 when the exporter's last collection cycle failed, so every cnpg_collector_* gauge is stale. During a rolling restart this is expected for a minute or two.
panels.title: Metric collection errors

panels.description: Seconds since the most recently started instance's postmaster came up. A small value on the primary means a restart or failover just happened.
panels.title: Postmaster uptime

panels.description: Start time per instance as a step plot: each step is a restart, and the primary is whichever line moved last after a failover.
panels.title: Instance postmaster start time

panels.description: How long each exporter collection cycle takes. It must stay far below the 30s scrape interval; approaching it means the collection queries themselves are a load problem.
panels.title: Metric collection duration

list.description: Instance pod (main-1/2/3). Only `cnpg_collector_up` carries a `cluster` label in CNPG 1.30, so scaling by pod is the filter that works across every family.
list.label: Instance
list.name: pod

title: CloudNativePG - cluster
